title: Clamp a part to the mill table with a strap clamp, its heel on the step-block tread that levels it
instruction: Clamp the blue part to the mill table with the red strap clamp.
context: Machinists and mill setup operators hold work with strap clamps: the heel rests on a step-block tread level with or just above the part, the stud sits nearer the part, and the nut is tightened last until the strap holds (O*NET 51-4041.00 Machinists; 51-4035.00 Milling and Planing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders). Board clamp tasks use vises, cams and bar clamps; none builds a level strap clamp from loose parts. This one adds choosing and placing the tread, threading a slotted strap onto a stud under the nut, then tightening the nut until the strap is held.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm). Heights are above the table. Table: oak top, arm bases 61 cm apart on its near edge. Mill table plate: dark grey steel, 22 x 16 x 1 cm, x 16 to 38, y -10 to 6, fixed. On it: blue anodised aluminium part, 6 x 6 x 4 cm, 390 g, centre x 20.2, y -2, against two fixed grey steel stops 1 cm thick and 2.5 cm tall, one on its -x face (x 16.2 to 17.2) and one on its -y face (y -6 to -5). Grey steel M12 x 1.75 threaded stud, rising to 13 cm, at x 27, y -2. On it, from the bottom: a lift spring (1.5 N per mm) under a grey steel spring washer, 2 x 4.4 cm, 40 g, top 5.4 cm up (4 mm above the part); a brass thrust washer, 20 g, keyed against turning, its 3.4 x 4.2 cm pad's underside 8.1 cm up (in the simulator it also carries the thread's stepped ramp, 6.6 cm across); an orange steel M12 flange nut, 2.6 cm across its flange, 60 g, underside 11.8 cm up, with a yellow handle 1.8 cm across and 2.8 cm tall, 5.5 cm from the stud's axis, at x 28.0, y 3.4, its foot 10 cm up. Turning the nut clockwise (seen from above) drives the thrust washer down the thread: 1.9 cm, about 11 turns, to reach a level strap. Overhead mill arm: grey steel bar 11 x 2 x 1.5 cm, 20 to 21.5 cm up, x 10 to 21, y -3 to -1, on a grey column 3 x 3 x 21.5 cm at x 11.5, y -2; it holds a black end mill, 1.6 cm across and 8 cm long, at x 20, y -2, its tip 12 cm up. Red anodised aluminium strap: bar 11.5 x 4.2 x 1.2 cm, 115 g, with a slot 1.8 cm wide and 7 cm deep open at one end, and a white grip tab 1.8 x 3 x 3 cm on top, 1 cm from the closed end; centre x 30, y -17, long side along x, slot end toward the arms. Yellow ABS plastic step block: 8 x 4 cm, 120 g, four 2 cm treads 2, 3, 4 and 5 cm tall (measured from its underside) rising in +x; centre x 24, y 15, long side along x.
scoring: Tools: top photo, ruler, spring scale. Score 0 if the part ever moved over 3 mm from its start, or the strap is off the table or held up (underside over 1 cm above every support). Else 1.0 if the strap is set and clamped; 0.5 if set only; 0.25 if its toe is over the part and its heel on any tread, tilted at most 15 degrees; else 0. Set: stud in the slot; 1.0 to 2.5 cm of toe over the part, at most 1 cm above it; heel end resting on the tread whose top is 0 to 4 mm above the part's top. Clamped: toe on the part (within 2 mm), heel end 0 to 4 mm above the toe, tilt at most 3 degrees, thrust washer on the strap (gap up to 1 mm), and held. Real test: a 5 N pull across the heel end moves it under 1 mm. Simulator: nut turned 110 degrees or more, washer depth matching it within 3 mm, lift spring pressed 3 mm or more (4.5 N): the nut's 3.8 N x friction 0.8 x 2 faces = 6 N.
reset_notes: Turn the nut back to its start (handle at x 28.0, y 3.4, thrust washer 8.1 cm up), put the part against both stops, and the strap and step block at their start spots.
fidelity: Approximate. The M12 thread is a coarse stepped helix worked by contact: a lug under the nut climbs 80 steps of 0.34 mm on the keyed thrust washer, so 140 degrees of turn stand for about 11 turns and the nut stays at one height while its washer travels. It holds because the lug rests on a flat step. The 5 N pull test is not run: the nut's angle and the lift spring's load are read instead. A strap more than 1 cm above every support is not placed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (moved the right arm over the strap area, never placed or clamped it); demo: 1.0 (placed the step block, set the strap on the stud, turned the nut, retreated)
